data.one_liner: A GraphQL client for Dart and Flutter with code generation and normalized caching.
data.what_it_does: Ferry is a GraphQL client that generates immutable data classes and provides typed cache reads and writes. It supports customizable network links, normalized optimistic caching with local persistence, pagination, and Flutter widgets for queries, mutations, and subscriptions.
use_when: You are building a Flutter or Dart app that communicates with a GraphQL API.
You need compile-time type safety for GraphQL operations, fragments, and cache updates.
You require a normalized cache with offline persistence using Hive.
avoid_when: Your project uses REST instead of GraphQL.
You want to avoid build-time code generation for your models.
strengths: Fully typed responses, operations, fragments, and cache reads/writes.
Built-in code generators for immutable data classes.
Normalized optimistic cache with offline persistence support via Hive.
weaknesses: Requires setting up build-runner and code generation.
Higher initial setup complexity compared to lightweight HTTP clients.
data.setup_notes: Requires code generation setup (build_runner) for generating operations and fragments based on your schema.
